—————————————————————————————

Many consumers assume that any product labeled as “sourdough” is inherently healthy and conducive to weight loss. However, this is often a misconception. To expedite production, many commercial bakeries utilize standard baker’s yeast to accelerate fermentation, adding artificial acidifiers simply to replicate the signature tangy flavor‼️

Purchasing these imitation sourdoughs deprives you of the metabolic and nutritional benefits of authentic fermentation. In terms of glycemic impact, they are virtually identical to conventional white bread—causing rapid blood sugar spikes and elevated insulin secretion, which promotes fat storage and can actively hinder your weight loss goals🫨

Given that both are made from flour, what gives authentic sourdough its low-glycemic index property?
The secret lies within the extended, multi-hour natural fermentation process:

1️⃣ The organic acids (specifically lactic and acetic acids) generated during slow fermentation delay gastric emptying, thereby slowing down the systemic absorption of carbohydrates.

2️⃣ The wild microorganisms pre-digest and break down a portion of the starches during fermentation, significantly lowering the overall glycemic response and providing prolonged satiety.

【🍌 水果 vs 零食，你會揀邊個？】

好多時大家見到水果糖分高，就會擔心會肥，但其實致肥唔係睇糖，而係睇每日總熱量同整體飲食習慣。

水果雖然含有天然果糖，但同時提供膳食纖維、水分、維他命、礦物質同抗氧化物，令血糖上升速度較平穩，食落去更容易有飽腹感🙌🏻

相反，零食和甜品通常由精製澱粉、砂糖同高脂肪組成，纖維含量低，容易導致血糖急升急跌📈長期多食更易增加肥胖和代謝疾病風險。

✅睇食物唔只睇糖分或卡路里，仲要睇營養價值。
✅食水果時可以配合堅果、乳酪或蛋白質，進一步減慢血糖上升。
✅零食可以偶爾享受，但唔好成為日常習慣。

水果係健康首選，零食最好少量或偶爾食，最重要係保持均衡飲食，咁樣唔單止可以滿足口癮同時又維持到健康既飲食習慣😉

Many people worry that eating fruit will make them gain weight because of its sugar content, but in reality, weight gain depends not on sugar alone, but on your total daily calorie intake and overall eating habits.

Fruits contain fructose, dietary fiber, and plenty of water, so they raise blood sugar slowly, help you feel full, and provide vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants 🍌

Snacks and desserts, on the other hand, are usually made with refined flour, sugar, and high fat, and contain little fiber, which can cause rapid spikes in blood sugar. Eating them frequently over the long term can increase the risk of obesity and metabolic diseases.

✅Don’t just look at sugar or calories—consider the nutritional value of foods.
✅Pair fruits with nuts, yogurt, or protein to slow down the rise in blood sugar.
✅Snacks can be enjoyed occasionally, but shouldn’t become a daily habit.

Fruits are the healthier choice, while snacks should be eaten sparingly or occasionally, so you can satisfy cravings while staying healthy😉

Egg Yolks Causing High Cholesterol? 
Eggs are rich in high-quality protein, vitamins D and E, folate, and Omega-3 fatty acids, offering numerous health benefits. However, many people worry that eating eggs will raise their cholesterol levels, sometimes choosing only the egg whites and avoiding the yolks. So, should we really eat eggs? And how many per day is appropriate? 🧐

💁🏻‍♀️ Most Cholesterol is Made by the Liver, Not from Food! In fact, our liver produces most of the cholesterol in our body; only a small portion comes from food. Even if you completely avoid eggs or other high-cholesterol foods, your liver will still produce cholesterol. Roughly 70-80% of cholesterol is synthesized by the liver, with only 20-30% coming from the diet. So, eating a moderate amount of high-cholesterol foods actually has minimal impact on your body’s cholesterol levels.

💡 The Real Concern: Saturated Fat! It’s saturated fat that raises bad cholesterol (LDL) levels, affecting cardiovascular health. It’s recommended to reduce foods high in saturated fats, such as fatty cuts of meat, and high-fat processed foods to help prevent high cholesterol levels‼️

Many people have heard the myth that microwave can produce harmful radiation that affects our health. But is this really true 🧐?

In fact:
🔸Microwave heating is very safe.
🔸Microwave heating preserves food nutrients better than many other cooking methods.
🔸What can be harmful is not the microwave radiation itself, but the containers used in the microwave!

I hope this information helps everyone understand microwaves better. Next time, I‘ll share some important tips about microwave-safe containers 🙋🏻‍♀️
